           Title: Theodosiani Libri XVI cum Constitutionibus
                  Sirmondianis et Leges Novellae ad Theodosianum
                  Pertinentes, Voluminis I Pars Posterior: Textus cum
                  Apparatu
      Creator(s): (Roman imperial legislation, 4th-5th c. CE, compiled
                  438 CE)
                  Th. Mommsen (Editor)
                  Paul M. Meyer (Editor)
     Print Basis: Berlin: Weidmann, 1905. Title page: "EDIDERUNT TH.
                  MOMMSEN et PAULUS M. MEYER."
          Rights: Public Domain
    Rights basis: This is a Google Books scan (via Internet Archive) of
                  the original volume, and the scan's own inserted
                  disclaimer page (kept below, not stripped) states
                  Google's own public-domain finding for this item
                  directly: "This is a digital copy of a book that was
                  preserved for generations on library shelves before it
                  was carefully scanned by Google... It has survived
                  long enough for the copyright to expire and the book
                  to enter the public domain." Independently, the 1905
                  publication date alone places this edition long out of
                  US copyright.
Source Collection: Internet Archive item theodosianilibr01sirmgoog,
                  fetched directly from
                  https://archive.org/download/theodosianilibr01sirmgoog/theodosianilibr01sirmgoog_djvu.txt
                  (2026-09-07, this session, direct network fetch - no
                  DOCX intermediate step). Because the file was pulled
                  from archive.org's own download endpoint rather than
                  its item webpage, there was no page-navigation chrome
                  (site header/menu, "Full text of ...", "See other
                  formats") to strip; the file below begins directly
                  with Google's own scanned disclaimer page, unedited.

     Acquisition history: this is the Donatism world-build's Manifest
                  §1 request G3, the Mommsen & Meyer critical edition.
                  Five prior attempts (2026-09-01) at this same edition
                  all returned a DIFFERENT archive.org item
                  (theodosianilibri02code / theodosianilibri00codeuoft),
                  which is Mommsen's Prolegomena in Theodosianum (Vol. I
                  Pars Prior - the manuscript-tradition and
                  textual-critical apparatus), not this Pars Posterior
                  text volume - see don_Decision_Log.md's 2026-09-01 G3
                  entries for the full account. A substitute source
                  (Boyd 1905, cic/texts/boyd_ecclesiastical-edicts-theodosian-code_1905.txt)
                  was vendored in the meantime; this file supplements,
                  not replaces, that substitute, since Boyd's own essay
                  does not quote law 16.5.52 verbatim or use the term
                  "agonistici."

     Content confirmed this session: all 16 Books present (Book XVI
                  heading "LIBER DECIMVS SEXTVS" located twice - once in
                  a summary listing, once at the actual Book XVI text).
                  Law XVI.5.52 (dated "412 Ian. 30" in the text's own
                  heading) located and confirmed to contain the exact
                  phrase "circumcelliones argenti pondo decem" (a
                  graduated fine schedule by social rank for Donatists
                  who do not return to the Catholic church, with
                  Circumcellions assessed in silver rather than gold
                  like the other ranks) - this closes the standing gap
                  Source_Acquisition_Manifest.md and Doc_02 §9 both
                  flagged (the 16.5.52 citation unheld in any vendored
                  text). The term "agonistici" does NOT appear anywhere
                  in this file (checked directly, zero matches) - it is
                  confirmed NOT to be Theodosian Code vocabulary; its
                  likely source is Augustine's own polemic (unverified
                  this session, a separate open item).
     OCR quality: Raw, uncorrected OCR of a 1905 Latin critical edition
                  with a dense textual apparatus and sigla. Expect
                  systematic OCR noise typical of this corpus's other
                  Google Books scans (e.g. "e"/"c" confusion,
                  "qooqle" for "google" in the front matter). Any
                  specific quotation drawn from this file needs visual
                  cross-check against its own surrounding context before
                  being relied on for a verbatim claim.

are  our  gateways  to  the  past,  representing  a  wealth  of  history,  culture  and  knowledge  that's  often  difficult  to  discover.

publisher  to  a  library  and  finally  to  you.
